thread:
incident-bot: paging: PROD KV cache size spiking and continuous-batching throughput cliff on api-prod-2. Observed sudden growth in prefix/prompt cache keys and upstream 5xx rate rising. Paging on-call.

incident-bot: symptom summary: 50% increase in token compute latency, KV store mem usage +3.2GB in 10m, 500 error rate up from 0.2% -> 3.7% (p50 latency +220ms). Possible trigger: recent batch config tweak rolled 09:28 UTC.

sara: i'm on it, oncall here. starting live triage. tagging eng-sre and runtime. @mike @jia can you take a look at the KV key churn and batching change?

mike: joining. pulling last hour of kv-metrics and batch traces. quick grep shows a huge jump in prefix keys with slightly different tokenizer fingerprints — looks like hash collisions or tokenization mismatch creating duplicate prefixes.

jia: noted. i saw a rollout at 09:28 that adjusted continuous_batch_window from 40ms -> 120ms for throughput. that would explain increased batch sizes but shouldn't produce new keys. sending config diff:
```yaml
- continuous_batch_window: 40ms
+ continuous_batch_window: 120ms
- kv_prefix_shard: 64
+ kv_prefix_shard: 64
```

mike: sharing quick query: `SELECT count(distinct prefix_key) FROM kv_cache WHERE created_at > now() - interval '15 minutes';` result: +420k distinct keys compared to baseline. majority contain weird whitespace/tokenizer artifacts.

ram: is there a prompt templating change? template drift + tokenizer change can create new prompt keys per-request. i recall a small templating change in the assistant-safety lib yesterday.

alex: CS: we've seen three customers complain about sporadic 500s and higher latency on chat endpoints. affected tenants appear to be high-qps trial accounts using recent templates. i'll notify them we're investigating and will share timeline.

sara: immediate mitigation plan suggestions? options: roll back batch window, throttle batch size, evict problematic kv prefixes, or revert tokenizer/template change. which is lowest risk?

mike: lowest blast radius: revert the batch window to previous value (40ms) and disable prefix caching for templates path while we triage. i can prepare a hotfix and quick canary.

jia: +1. runtime will also flip `kv_prefix_cache_enabled=false` for route /v1/chat for 5% of traffic to measure impact. canary id C-4391.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued by mike: `hotfix/revert-batch-window` -> staging passed -> promoted to canary.

mike: rolling canary now to 3% of prod. watching metrics.

(2m later)

mike: canary looks good: kv distinct keys growth flattened on canary hosts, 5xx dropped from 3.7% -> 0.6% on canary traffic.

sara: good. schedule full rollback? risk of cascading restarts? how long to ramp?

jia: recommend staged rollback over 10 min: 3% -> 15% -> 50% -> 100%. i'll coordinate autoscaler and ensure no extra cache thrash. also we'll keep `kv_prefix_cache_enabled=false` for templates path until we confirm template/tokenizer drift root cause.

ram: i'm collecting sample prompt strings that generated the new keys. early look: some templates have unescaped zero-width spaces and a new tokenizer patch bumped tokenization changes (v2.11.4). mismatch between model-frontend tokenizer and runtime tokenizer produced different prefix hashes.

mike: that explains it — hash fingerprint changed so previously cached prefixes became new keys repeatedly, causing cache blowup and higher memory + IO. continuous batching then amplified pressure by combining many variant keys into large batches and evicting hot entries.

alex: CS update: posted to affected customers, said temporary rollback and we expect improvement within 15-30 minutes, offering status updates.

kyle: ops note: we're increasing KV node write throughput headroom while rolling back to avoid write throttles during rehydration. also bumping cache eviction TTL to buy time.

(rollout proceeds)

mike: 15m into rollback: metrics trending down. global 5xx at 0.9%, p50 latency back to baseline +30ms. kv mem steady.

sara: nice. now next steps for root cause:
- revert tokenizer version mismatch (pin tokenizers lib)
- audit template changes for unescaped whitespace and canonicalization
- add a safety check: if prefix frequency suddenly increases by X, auto-disable continuous batching for that route
- create postmortem and customer-impact summary

ram: i'll open PR to pin tokenizer to v2.11.3 across runtime + frontends. also adding a prompt canonicalizer to normalize zero-width spaces and trimmed whitespace before hashing.

jia: runtime follow-ups: add circuit-breaker to batch window rollback path and add a metric that emits `prefix_key_new_rate` and triggers an alert at 3x baseline.

mike: ops follow-ups: create a one-click runbook to disable continuous batching per-route and evict prefix cache keys matching regex. adding runbook entry now: https://runbooks.internal/revert-continuous-batch

deploy-bot: PR merged: `pin/tokenizer-v2.11.3` by ram. CI passed. scheduling deploy to canary for tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

alex: customers updated with expected timeline. offering credits to those who saw degraded SLAs.

sara: summary for postmortem: trigger = tokenizer/docs/template drift + batch window increase -> fingerprint mismatch -> prefix cache key blowup -> kv memory + write amplification -> continuous-batching amplified throughput and caused transient 5xx and latency. mitigations: rollback batch window, temporarily disable prefix cache on affected route, pin tokenizer, canonicalize templates, improve alerting & runbook.

mike: moving to incident review. assigning postmortem owners: ram (cause), jia (runtime mitigations), kyle (ops + capacity), alex (customer comms). i'll close pager in 30m unless regression. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sara: handing off to night on-call at 23:00 UTC. leaving notes in #oncall-handoffs. if anything spikes again, wake me.

alex: added customer impact doc with timestamps and affected tenant ids (internal tracker). will share with sales as needed.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. incident severity: Sev2 -> update by postmortem.

mike: closing thread for now, uploading logs and span traces to /incidents/2190001234/artifacts.

sara: thanks all, good coordination.
